newsitem.title: USA: CGT sees northern Va. gas line back today.
newsitem.headline: CGT sees northern Va. gas line back today.

text.p: Columbia Gas Transmission Corp (CGT) said Tuesday it expected to restore service later today on a 30-inch diameter natural gas line through northern Virginia after finding a leak on the line this morning.
"It looks like the pipeline is probably going to be back in service later today," said company spokeswoman Alma Adkins.
The line was flowing 350,000 cubic feet of gas a day (mmcfd) at the time of the outage, she said.
Traders said spot gas prices on Columbia Gulf were unchanged from Monday following news of the outage, holding in a range of $1.78-1.80 per million British thermal units (mmBtu).
Adkins said the leak occured on the VC1 pipeline section running from CGT's compression station in Loudoun County, Va.
Only that section of the line was shut, she added.
"We're not sure what caused the leak. But it was not a line break and it was not an explosion. It looks like it's just a gasket between two flanges," she said.
CGT operates an extensive, 19,000-mile network of natural gas pipelines across the eastern U.S.
CGT is a subsidiary of The Columbia Gas System, Inc.
